_metadata.description: Entity-level, foreign-qualification and excise obligations that are NOT ordinary sales-tax remittance. Each rule carries its applicability condition, a due-date RULE (never a hardcoded date), a confidence tag and an official source.
_metadata.disclaimer: Monitoring aid only. Not legal or tax advice. Amounts and dates change; last_reviewed tells you how stale a rule is.

applies_when_values.home_state: the profile's home_state matches this state
applies_when_values.sales_tax_registered: nexus_status.is_registered is true for this state
applies_when_values.user_confirmed: only when enabled_obligations['XX:type'] is explicitly true — never scheduled automatically
applies_when_values.wildcard_state: state_code '*' is a fallback applied to every foreign_qualified state that has no specific rule of the same obligation_type

due_rule_kinds.fixed_month_day: same calendar date every year (uses month/day)
due_rule_kinds.months_after_year_end: N months after fiscal year end, on a given day
due_rule_kinds.anniversary: anniversary of a profile date (formation_date or qualified_date)
due_rule_kinds.biennial_frequency: frequency 'biennial' generates only in years matching the anchor date's parity

obligations.title: Maryland Annual Report (+ Business Personal Property Return if applicable)
obligations.amount_note: $300 annual report filing fee for an LLC. A Business Personal Property Return must be filed WITH the annual report if the entity owns/leases personal property in Maryland or maintains a Maryland trader's licence — answer SDAT's two threshold questions to confirm.

source.authority: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
source.citation: Form 1 — Annual Report and Business Personal Property Return

obligations.notes: All domestic and foreign entities formed, qualified or registered in Maryland must file the Annual Report. Late filing draws a penalty of 1/10 of 1% of the county assessment plus interest. This is an SDAT filing and is entirely separate from any Comptroller sales-and-use tax return.

obligations.title: Oklahoma LLC Annual Certificate (foreign LLC)
obligations.due_rule_text: On the anniversary date of the LLC's Oklahoma registration each year.

source.citation: Limited Liability Company Annual Certificate (SOS Form)

obligations.notes: A foreign LLC registered to do business in Oklahoma files an annual certificate each year on its anniversary date, confirming it is active and stating its principal place of business and e-mail address. Oklahoma's separate corporate franchise tax was repealed for periods after 2023 — verify current status with a CPA before assuming any franchise filing is still required.

obligations.title: California $800 minimum LLC annual tax
obligations.due_rule_text: 15th day of the 4th month OF the taxable year — April 15 for a calendar-year LLC, i.e. during the year it covers, not after it. A first-year LLC's $800 is due the 15th day of the 4th month after filing its articles, so the first year needs checking by hand.
obligations.amount_note: $800 minimum annual tax. LLCs with California-source income over $250,000 owe an additional fee ($900–$11,790). Form 568 is the annual return and has its own deadline.
obligations.confidence_note: The $800 amount and due-date rule are high confidence. Whether THIS entity is 'doing business' in California is the contested part — that is why the obligation is review-only until confirmed.

source.citation: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 17941, 23101; multiple OTA decisions 2019–2024

obligations.notes: The FTB treats FBA inventory storage in California as 'doing business', and the OTA has sustained that position. It is administered by the FTB, not the CDTFA, so registering for California sales tax does not address it. This is deliberately NOT auto-scheduled: it turns on a legal position about this specific entity. Confirm with a CPA, then set enabled_obligations['CA:franchise_tax'] = true to start tracking the fee.

obligations.title: Hawaii GET annual return / reconciliation
obligations.due_rule_text: 20th day of the 4th month following the close of the taxable year (April 20 for a calendar-year filer).

source.citation: Form G-49, Annual Return and Reconciliation of General Excise / Use Tax Return

obligations.notes: Hawaii's General Excise Tax is a tax on the business, not a sales tax on the buyer, and it works as two filings: periodic G-45 returns plus an annual G-49 reconciliation. The G-45 periodics are already tracked in filing_calendar under Hawaii's assigned frequency; only the G-49 is added here, so the two are never double-counted.

obligations.title: Kentucky Secretary of State annual report
obligations.due_rule_text: By June 30 each year (filing window opens January 1).
obligations.notes: Required of entities registered with the Kentucky Secretary of State. Missing June 30 leads to administrative dissolution. NOTE: this is an entity-registration obligation — being registered for Kentucky SALES TAX does not by itself create it, which is why it is gated on foreign qualification rather than on nexus_status.

obligations.title: Kentucky Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET)
obligations.due_rule_text: Generally the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the taxable year — CONFIRM against the form instructions for the entity's filing type before relying on it.
obligations.confidence_note: The $175 minimum is confirmed by the Department of Revenue. Whether a remote/FBA seller with no Kentucky presence beyond inventory is 'doing business' for LLET purposes is NOT settled here, and the exact due date depends on the entity's filing form. Review-only until a CPA confirms.

source.citation: Corporation Income and Limited Liability Entity Tax; Schedule LLET

obligations.notes: Deliberately not auto-scheduled. Kentucky was called out as 'verify what actually applies; do not assume' — this rule records what was verified (the $175 minimum exists) and what was not (that it applies to this entity).

obligations.form_code: Franchise Tax Report + Public Information Report
obligations.title: Texas franchise tax report and PIR
obligations.amount_note: No tax due below the no-tax-due revenue threshold, but the Public Information Report is still required of entities registered with the Comptroller.
obligations.confidence_note: The May 15 date is high confidence. Whether this entity has a Texas franchise-tax filing requirement depends on whether it is registered with the Comptroller / has nexus — confirm before scheduling.
obligations.notes: Already represented in config/seed_franchise_rules.json as a review flag; this entry adds the schedulable form once the user confirms the entity is registered with the Comptroller.

obligations.title: Nevada Commerce Tax
obligations.due_rule_text: 45 days after the June 30 fiscal year end (on or about August 14) — CONFIRM the current date with the Department of Taxation.
obligations.amount_note: Applies only to Nevada gross revenue above $4,000,000 for the fiscal year.
obligations.confidence_note: Deliberately low. The threshold is high, most sellers are below it, and the filing-requirement-below-threshold rules have changed. This exists to keep Nevada OUT of the sales-tax calendar as a phantom quarterly return, not to assert a filing is owed.
obligations.notes: Never auto-scheduled. Nevada's commerce tax is an annual gross-receipts tax with a $4M threshold and must not be turned into quarterly sales-tax dues.

obligations.title: Delaware annual LLC tax
obligations.due_rule_text: June 1 each year, for the prior year.
obligations.amount_note: $300 annual tax. Delaware does NOT require an annual report from an LLC — the tax is the whole obligation. Late payment draws a $200 penalty plus 1.5%/month interest. One Division of Corporations page mentions a $400 figure; confirm the current amount when paying.
obligations.notes: Applies to all domestic AND foreign LLCs formed or registered in Delaware. Despite the 'franchise tax' name this is a flat annual tax, not income-based.

obligations.title: Florida LLC annual report
obligations.due_rule_text: Filing window opens January 1; due by May 1.
obligations.amount_note: $138.75 if filed between January 1 and May 1. A $400 late fee applies after May 1 and is not waivable.

source.authority: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations

obligations.notes: Required of domestic and foreign LLCs registered in Florida to keep 'active' status. The first report is due in the year following registration.

obligations.title: California Statement of Information (biennial)
obligations.due_rule_text: Within 90 days of first registering, then every 2 years by the end of the calendar MONTH of the original registration date. The engine dates it to the registration day within that month; the state's deadline is the month end, so treat this as the earliest date, not the last.
obligations.amount_note: Filing fee not verified here — check the Secretary of State fee schedule before paying.
obligations.confidence_note: The biennial cadence and month-end rule are confirmed by the Secretary of State. The exact day within the month and the fee are not, so this is medium rather than high.

source.citation: Statements of Information — filing tips (Form LLC-12)

obligations.notes: Entirely separate from the FTB $800 franchise tax, which stays review-only. This is a Secretary of State registration filing and applies only once the LLC is actually qualified in California.

obligations.title: Foreign-qualification annual report — generic
obligations.due_rule_text: PLACEHOLDER: dated to the qualification anniversary because most states use one. Many do not — some use a fixed calendar date, some are biennial. VERIFY with that state's Secretary of State and add a specific rule.
obligations.confidence_note: Deliberately low. This is a reminder that a foreign-qualified state almost certainly has SOME annual obligation, not a claim about what it is or when it is due. It exists so adding a state to foreign_qualified never silently tracks nothing.

source.citation: No official source; replace with a state-specific rule

obligations.notes: Applies only to foreign-qualified states with no specific rule in this file. When you verify a state, add a proper entry above and this fallback stops applying to it automatically.
